ms.report:
Sorry for that. The permissions have been given to the doc.

Also, you are right; clarifying the scenarios a bit better was necessary.

On the one hand, using either our UI directly or the API provided by our server, both paths trigger the backend service that monitors the network until it confirms the transaction and synchronizes the database. These paths do not require additional manual action from the users other than signing and submitting the transaction.

On the other hand, webhooks are the most efficient way to monitor the network because their servers are usually always active and online, and they can trigger upon transactions created outside our system (for example, transactions created with Cardano CLI commands).

If we want to have a webhook on our servers to avoid relying on external services, it would be important to have a node as well. Without a node, this webhook would have to periodically make requests to services like Blockfrost to get information about each monitored address. Ideally, to avoid external dependencies, the best scenario is to have a node running on our servers.

In any case, for these examples, we do not activate these webhooks, either externally or as an internal service. However, the mechanisms are present. We have an API URL that can be called whenever there is an update. This URL is what we would provide to a webhook to call our server and trigger synchronization. This URL is the same one called by the "Sync" button still present in the provided example, which we used for manual synchronization. That button calls a specific URL to trigger synchronization. Therefore, in webhook services, you can call that same API.

The URL in question, for example, to trigger synchronization when there are new transactions on an address using the provided API is:

http://localhost:3000/api/dummy/sync/<ADDRESS>

Thanks!

Implement transaction creation logic considering the UTxO model and datum handling. There will be API endpoints for each transaction that will be in charge of create the CBOR code in the backend. The user will get the CBOR code ready to sign in the front end. 
Develop mechanisms to handle in-use UTxOs for preventing concurrency issues. All the UTXOs in the database will have a flag switched when they are part of some ongoing transaction. If there are more that one UTXO possible to choose, the system will then try to get one that is not being used by other user in the same time. 
Design and implement read-only access to UTxOs for other users. Users can still access and see the content of flawed UTXOs. Also if a transaction is using a UTXO as reference input, this UTXO will be still accessible to others users that needed to use them as reference as well, but not accessible if the they require them to consume.
Test and validate transaction processing and concurrency features.

Milestone 05 Report
Smart DB Concurrency and Transaction Management
Introduction
This document outlines the key features and implementations delivered in Milestone 05 of the Smart DB project. The focus has been on enhancing transaction creation logic, implementing robust concurrency handling mechanisms, and introducing a smart UTxO system to optimize blockchain interactions on the Cardano platform. This milestone demonstrates significant improvements in managing concurrent transactions and efficient UTxO selection.

Key Implementations
1. Entity Structure and Relationships
Free Entity
・Extends SmartDBEntity, representing data that exists both in the local database and on the Cardano blockchain.
・Used as a test case for demonstrating the smart UTxO selection system and concurrency handling.
・Has a one-to-one relationship with a SmartUTxO Entity, linking blockchain data with local metadata.

SmartUTxO Entity
・Represents UTxOs in the system, stored in a dedicated database table.
・Contains detailed information about UTxO location on the blockchain and its current usage state.
・Includes timestamps fields: isPreparingForReading, isReading, isPreparingForConsuming, and isConsuming for concurrency management.

Transaction Entity
・Stored in a separate database table to track all transactions in the system.
・Used to manage transaction lifecycle and status updates.
・Includes statuses like CREATED, PENDING, SUBMITTED, CONFIRMED, FAILED, etc.
・Essential for handling concurrency and synchronizing database state with blockchain.

These entities work together to enable efficient concurrency handling, UTxO management, and blockchain synchronization.

A dedicated page (http://localhost:3000/concurrency) in the application showcases the concurrency features:
・Wallet connection and balance display.
・Creation, updating, and deletion of Free entities.
・Real-time display of UTxO statuses, including preparation and consumption states.

Milestone 06 Report
Introduction
This document outlines the key features and implementations delivered in Milestone 06 of the Smart DB project. The milestone focuses on optimizing data retrieval, implementing efficient query management, and improving overall system performance.
Key Implementations
1. Optimized Data Retrieval
・Selective Field Retrieval: Implemented a mechanism to retrieve only necessary fields from the database for each query, minimizing data transfer and improving performance.
・Sorting and Limiting: Added parameters to all APIs, allowing users to specify sorting criteria and limit the number of records returned.
・Optimized and Non-Optimized Entity Testing: Added a product entity with multiple fields as a performance test case to analyze optimizations and retrieve times comparatively.

2. Queries Management
・Database Indexes: Created appropriate database indexes on frequently queried fields and columns involved in join operations, optimizing query performance and ensuring efficient data retrieval.
・Covered Queries: Utilized covered indexes to minimize I/O operations, allowing the database to execute queries entirely from the index, avoiding additional table lookups.

3. Data Caching and Metadata Management
・Token Metadata Table: Introduced a dedicated table to store metadata retrieved from BlockFrost API, which eliminates the need for repeated metadata requests, reducing dependency on external sources and increasing system responsiveness.
・Caching Mechanism Adjustment: Initial plans included caching techniques for datums and redeemers. However, based on the team’s accumulated experience, these techniques were determined to be unnecessary for this project phase, as explained below.

Technical Details
Selective Field Retrieval
Implemented a flexible query builder that allows users to specify desired fields in their requests, leading to improved performance in data retrieval and reducing data transfer load.
